lessons.title: Getting ready to mow safely
lessons.html:
Getting ready to mow safely

A neat lawn makes a garden look good. Mowing cuts the grass to the same height all over. But a lawnmower is a dangerous machine. The blade turns very fast. It can cut off toes and throw stones like bullets. Always get ready properly before you start.

Your protective clothing

  • Safety boots with steel toes. Never mow in sandals or barefoot.
  • Long trousers.
  • Safety glasses to protect your eyes from stones and grass.
  • Ear protection, because mowers are loud.
  • A hat and sunscreen on hot days.

Check the lawn first

Walk over the whole lawn before you mow. Pick up:

  • Stones, sticks and bones
  • Toys, hoses and wire
  • Dog mess and rubbish

Look for sprinkler heads, tap boxes and small walls. Mark them or remember where they are, so you do not hit them.

Check the mower

  1. The mower must be switched off. For a petrol mower, pull the spark plug lead off before you touch the blade.
  2. Check the blade is sharp and not bent or loose. Tell your team leader if it is damaged.
  3. Check the guards and grass box are in place.
  4. For a petrol mower, fill fuel outside, with the engine cold. Do not smoke. Wipe up spills.
  5. For an electric mower, check the cable for cuts. Keep the cable behind you while you mow.
  6. Set the cutting height your team leader tells you.

People and animals

Ask people, children and pets to move away from the lawn. Stop the mower at once if anyone comes close.

lessons.title: Mowing and finishing off
lessons.html:
Mowing and finishing off

Cutting height

Do not cut the grass too short. Short grass burns in the sun, dries out and lets weeds grow. A good rule is to cut off only the top third of the grass each time. Kikuyu and Cynodon lawns can be cut shorter than buffalo grass, which likes to be longer. Your team leader will tell you the height for each lawn.

How to mow

  1. Start the mower on flat ground, with your feet away from the blade.
  2. Mow around the edge of the lawn first.
  3. Then mow in straight lines, up and down. Overlap each line a little so no strips are left.
  4. Walk at a steady speed. Push the mower; never pull it towards your feet.
  5. On a slope, mow across the slope with a push mower, never up and down.
  6. Empty the grass box before it is too full.
  7. Change direction each time you mow the lawn, so the grass grows straight.

Never

  • Never lift or tilt a running mower.
  • Never put your hand or foot under the mower while it is running.
  • Never mow wet grass if you can avoid it. It is slippery and clogs the mower.
  • Never leave a running mower alone.

Finishing

  • Trim edges with an edge cutter or shears.
  • Sweep or blow clippings off paths and paving.
  • Put clippings on the compost heap, in thin layers.
  • Clean the mower when it is off and cool. Scrape grass from under the deck, with the spark plug lead off.
  • Store the mower in the shed.

Key points

  • Wear safety boots, glasses and ear protection.
  • Clear stones and rubbish from the lawn first.
  • Cut off only the top third of the grass.
  • Mow in straight, overlapping lines; across slopes.
  • Never touch the blade unless the mower is off and the spark plug lead is removed.
